title: Purpose Codes
sectionDescription: Collecting money and the objects it touches.
entryDescription: The fixed regulator-defined purpose codes for payins and payouts.
content:
# Purpose Codes

Purpose codes come from a fixed, regulator-defined set. Do not invent a value; use the published list. Purpose codes are grouped by category, and each category carries several codes with a description and the documents required to support a payment of that kind. When you build a payin you must pass a purpose code that matches the underlying reason for the transfer, because the regulator reconciles the declared purpose against the supporting documents. Choosing the wrong code delays settlement and can trigger a request for information. The categories cover trade in goods, trade in services, remittances, capital flows and a handful of specialised cases. For most e-commerce merchants collecting for goods sold to overseas customers, the relevant category is trade in goods. The service equivalents cover software, consulting and other intangibles. Remittance categories cover family maintenance and similar personal transfers, which most merchants will not use. Capital-flow categories are restricted and generally require additional approval. Each code is a short alphanumeric identifier. The code for receiving payment for physical goods exported from India is P1006. Pass it exactly as written; the value is case sensitive and must not be abbreviated or reformatted.

title: Webhooks
entryDescription: Event catalogue, signature verification and retry semantics.
content:
# Webhooks

Verify the X-Glomopay-Signature header using HMAC SHA-256 before processing any webhook payload.
